calls.reason: The only evidence is Perplexity's ad launch in late 2024 and small payouts to publishers. Neither gives free-user revenue or serving costs, so whether free users were a net cost can't be judged.
No figures on Google's cost or revenue per prompt exist in the packet. Gemini's 90M monthly users in Oct 2024 trailed its rivals but still ranked second in an NBER survey, so the evidence is mixed.
OpenAI's $122B committed round in March 2026 shows capital raised, not capital needed to keep the Feb 2025 business going. Nothing separates upkeep from expansion, and no deadline was given.

Epoch AI's estimate puts 2024 compute at $3B for training and $1.8B for inference, against about $3.7B revenue. That is a gap of roughly $1.1B, and Epoch says the figures look approximately correct despite partly projected Q4 numbers.

'No moat' is a loose judgement call. DeepSeek-R1 shows competitors catching up on capability, while Claude's reach through Amazon Bedrock hints at an advantage. Neither source measures switching costs or how lasting any advantage is.

Reporting cited by Fortune put OpenAI's paid-user compute margin at 52% at the end of 2024. FutureSearch separately estimated API gross margins of 55-75% in mid-2024. Whole categories of prompts covered their serving costs, against 'every single prompt'.
